segments.line: It's nine forty- seven on a Tuesday night.
You're on the roof with your best friend Mo and a borrowed telescope,
because your little sister Ellie needs a drawing of the full Moon for school.
You look down to sharpen your pencil.
There's just a round, black hole in the sky where it used to be.
Down the street, every dog starts barking at once.
Every phone in the neighborhood lights up.
Mo slowly lowers the telescope. 'Okay, ' he says.
And by the next morning, the ocean at the end of your street hasn't come back in.
So what would really happen if the Moon disappeared tonight? The
first night, the first year, and a million years from now.
